Peraso validates a 60 GHz humanoid-to-edge link at about 500 Mbps uplink

The demonstration keeps urgent responses on a local GPU while a remote cluster handles more demanding models.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗21 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Wireless link validation

Peraso announced a functional validation on October 21 connecting a humanoid to an edge AI server over 60 GHz wireless. It reports sustained throughput of approximately 500 Mbps from robot to server and 100 Mbps in the reverse direction for video, sensors and operational data.

Splitting local and remote computation

The demonstration uses a local NVIDIA GPU for urgent, low-latency responses and a remote GPU cluster for more demanding models. This reduces the need to run every model onboard, while system design must still address connectivity limitations.

The demonstration has a defined scope

Directional beamforming is intended to reduce interference between nearby links. A separately cited 50 Gbps aggregate result came from an earlier demonstration, not this robot’s link. End-to-end latency and long-term factory reliability results are not disclosed.
